text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NEWS
- The Pakistan Muslim League government is set to announce a record low increase in defence allocations in the 1997/98 (July-June) budget.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto said the inquiry commission has not identified who was involved in the murder conspiracy of her brother Murtaza Bhutto.
THE MUSLIM
- Pakistan plans to hold a seven-nation moot on the Afghan crisis in Islamabad next month.
THE NATION
- The government will set an increased revenue collection target of 328 billion rupees in the 1997/98 (July-June) budget.
- Pakistan has been advised by the International Monetary Fund to continue structural reforms and take strong stabilisation measures.
DAWN
- Many members of the Pakistan Muslim League parliamentary party in the Punjab province opposed the government's decision to impose agricultural tax, saying farmers were not in a position to pay it.

- A meeting presided over by Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz has decided in principle not to impose new taxes and manage the current weak funding position by having a very restricted development programme.

- Europe's cotton manufacturers have tabled a new complaint against imports of grey cloth or unbleached cotton from Pakistan and other countries, alleging that the products are being "dumped" on their markets.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif is to address the nation on June 11 on the prevailing economic and political situation.

- Pakistan Railways plans to increase fares at least 10 percent, discontinue 140 passenger services and close four sleeper manufacturing units to bridge a gap of over 1.0 billion rupees expected after the government ends its subsidy.
- The Central Board of Revenue will submit its tax collection target for the financial year 1997/98 on Tuesday to the pre-budget receipts analysis committee.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Sindh province Chief Minister Liaquat Jatoi will present the provincial budget for 1997/98 (July-June) on June 16.
- The Privatisation Commission has changed the bidding procedure for Habib Credit and Exchange Bank Limited to be held on June 12 to make the process transparent and attractive.
